newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end 2.4 pct lower on margin loan calls.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end 2.4 pct lower on margin loan calls.

text.p: Seoul shares provisionally ended Friday's trading 15.82 points, or 2.4 percent, lower at 642.08 as the market's recent decline triggered margin loan calls, brokers said.

The issuance of margin loan calls further eroded investor confidence, leading to more sales of small and mid-sized shares. Investors bought many of those shares last October on margin accounts, they said.

After the 650 support line gave way this afternoon, selling snowballed. "Most margin loans are due in March or April. Those who had bought on the margin started worrying about a crash and sold out today," said Kevin Choi, a fund manager at Seoul Investment Trust Co. "
Declining shares eclipsed advancers 719 to 131. Volume was a moderate 27.57 million shares.
The decline, though concentrated on smaller shares, was across the board. Kukje fell 230 won to 5,400 and Chungwon lost 500 won to 7,720.
The market's mid-term outlook continued to be poor because fundamentals, including high interest rates, a faltering won and a slowing economy, did not bode well for a recovery.
"The economic environment is full of bad news, making it hard for the KOSPI to maintain any uptrend," Choi added.
Blue chips fell. LG Electronics declined fell 700 won to 9,700. Yukong shed 900 won to 14,000, and Korea Mobile Telecom lost 14,500 to 452,000.
Several bank shares saw active selling. Hana Bank declined 100 won to 11,200 in active trading. SEOULBANK fell 60 won to 3,200.
However, some brokers said a brief technical rebound was possible next week due to the steepness of Friday's decline.
